description.value: The study examined age-related similarities and differences in the neural mechanisms of cognitive reappraisal and tested whether individual cognitive abilities predicted regulation-related brain activation.

design.value: Twenty older and 22 younger adults completed psychometric testing and training in one session, followed on a different day by an fMRI cognitive reappraisal task involving positive, negative, and neutral pictures and Experience versus Reappraise conditions.

description.value: Screening measure of cognitive state; participants scored 27 or above.

Battery including immediate, delayed and recognition memory, simple and choice reaction time, Stroop, and forward and backward digit span; a composite z score was derived from mean performance across measures.
Self-report measure with reappraisal and suppression subscales.
Participants rated how negative or positive each image was at the end of each trial.

source_definition.value: a single composite score was derived based on mean performance across all measures

association_direction.value: negative for bilateral amygdala activation during negative stimuli; positive for LIFG activation during positive stimuli

description.value: Participants between the ages of 19 and 33 years.

medical_condition.value: no history of neurological or psychiatric disorder

diagnostic_instrument.value: Mini-Mental State Examination score of 27 or above

description.value: Participants between the ages of 59 and 73 years.

medical_condition.value: no history of neurological or psychiatric disorder

diagnostic_instrument.value: Mini-Mental State Examination score of 27 or above

task_description.value: Each trial began with a positive, negative, or neutral photographic image. Participants either experienced their emotions naturally or attempted to decrease their emotional response by reappraising the image.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally or to decrease their emotional response to the image by reappraising it, using an emotionally detached and objective third-party strategy.

stimuli.value: Positive, neutral, and negative images drawn from the International Affective Picture System.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported affective valence using an 8-option non-verbal Manikin scale

description.value: Functional data were collected across six runs, each containing 238 imaging volumes. An initial high-resolution inversion-recovery-prepared SPGR anatomical scan was acquired for co-registration and normalization.

structured_details.value: {"field_of_view":"240 mm","flip_angle":"90°","slices":"34 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane","anatomical_scan":"whole-brain coverage with approximately 1 mm3 voxel size"}

description.value: Pre-statistics processing included motion correction, slice-timing correction, removal of non-brain voxels, spatial smoothing, high-pass temporal filtering, run exclusion based on head motion, registration to high-resolution anatomical images, and normalization to the MNI template.

software.value: FEAT Version 5.98, part of FSL (FMRIB's Software Library)

steps.value: removal of non-brain voxels using BET
spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of FWHM 6 mm
runs with more than five volumes with greater than 1 mm of movement in any direction were excluded
registration to high-resolution anatomical images and normalization to the Montreal Neurologic Institute template using FLIRT

model_settings.value: Five regressors of interest modeled Experience-Positive, Experience-Negative, Experience-Neutral, Reappraise-Positive, and Reappraise-Negative; nuisance regressors modeled visual presentation and response periods. Whole-brain corrected thresholds were voxel z > 2.3 and cluster P < 0.05.

Left and right amygdala activation time courses, a regulation-condition boxcar waveform weighted positively for Reappraise and negatively for Experience, and two amygdala-by-task interaction regressors were included.
Relationships between regulation-related ROI activation changes and the cognitive composite score were tested while controlling for age.

description.value: Participants experienced the emotions evoked by the image naturally.
Participants attempted to decrease their emotional response to the image by reappraising it.
Positive images with standardized valence rating M = 7.3.
Negative images with standardized valence rating M = 2.5.
Neutral images with standardized valence rating M = 5.1; all neutral trials were Experience trials.

name.value: Reappraise > experience, positive images, collapsed across age groups

model_representation_notes.value: Five regressors of interest modeled the 8-s period using a unit amplitude function; additional nuisance regressors modeled the 2-s visual presentation and response period; regressors were convolved with a double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Reappraisal of positive images evoked increased activation in dorsolateral and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex and inferior parietal lobule.

name.value: Reappraise > experience, negative images, collapsed across age groups

model_representation_notes.value: Five regressors of interest modeled the 8-s period using a unit amplitude function; additional nuisance regressors modeled the 2-s visual presentation and response period; regressors were convolved with a double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: A similar pattern of activation was found when examining trials involving negative images.

name.value: Experience > reappraise, positive images, collapsed across age groups

model_representation_notes.value: Five regressors of interest modeled the 8-s period using a unit amplitude function; additional nuisance regressors modeled the 2-s visual presentation and response period; regressors were convolved with a double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Positive Experience trials, compared to positive Reappraise trials, evoked increased activation in regions including bilateral amygdala, mid-cingulate cortex, bilateral post-central gyrus and pregenual cortex.

name.value: Experience > reappraise, negative images, collapsed across age groups

model_representation_notes.value: Five regressors of interest modeled the 8-s period using a unit amplitude function; additional nuisance regressors modeled the 2-s visual presentation and response period; regressors were convolved with a double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Negative Experience trials, compared to negative Reappraise trials, revealed activations in amygdala, post-central gyrus and putamen, all bilaterally.
